Delta.description: One live frame of a session's response as it arrives, the data of an event: delta frame. A frame of text is {subagent, turn, step, block, kind, text}: text is the next run of the content block's text, thinking or tool input, to append to what the step's earlier deltas carried for that block. A reset is {subagent, turn, step, reset}: the step's request is sent again, so what its deltas carried is discarded. Deltas are best effort: never appended, never replayed, and dropped rather than slowing the turn; the step's agent.message is the record, so a client that misses deltas loses nothing, and a delta of a step whose agent.message the client holds is stale.

text.description: At most 1024 bytes; a longer run arrives as several deltas.

get.description: List the sessions of the agents of the caller's context, filtered by agent, status, runner and archived, newest first by id. A fork names the session it was forked from as parent {session_id, seq} and the session at the top of its fork tree as root; a session no fork made has neither, and its tree is keyed by its own id. root, parent and group narrow what the other filters and the authorizer's owners keep, so a tree's sessions the caller may not list are in no answer and no count. root lists a tree, parent a session's forks, and group=tree one session per tree: the newest of the tree's sessions the list keeps, the one with the greatest id, carrying tree {root, sessions}, root the tree's key and sessions how many of the tree's sessions the list keeps. A grouped list orders and pages by the id of each tree's newest session, so a fork moves its tree to the head of the list. A group other than tree is invalid_request. metadata.<key>=<value>, one such parameter per request, keeps the sessions whose metadata holds key with exactly value, beside every other filter and within the owners the authorizer's decision names; under group=tree a tree stands for itself when one of its sessions holds the entry. A second such parameter, a key that breaks the key rule of a create's metadata, and an empty value are invalid_request naming the parameter. trigger=<id>, a trigger's id, keeps the sessions that trigger started, those whose trigger_id it is, beside every other filter and the cursor, within the agents of the caller's context and the owners the authorizer's decision names; under group=tree a tree stands for itself when one of its sessions the trigger started, and a fork, which no trigger starts, is not kept by it. The id of no trigger, and of another context's trigger, keeps none of the caller's sessions. A value that is not a trigger's id is invalid_request. rollout=<id>, a rollout's id, keeps that rollout's runs, and rollout=any every session; absent, the runs of every rollout are left out, beside every other filter. Any other value is invalid_request.

post.description: Create a session of an agent, named by id or by name among the agents of the caller's context. The body's attended, true when a person answers the session's questions through a client that shows them, is the session's from its create on and nothing changes it: an agent's question then waits, the session idle with stop_reason question, until a user.answer, a person's user.message or a user.interrupt closes it, holding no runner while it waits; absent or false, a question is answered at once with outcome unanswered and the agent decides, so a client that shows no questions never meets one. The body's metadata is an object of at most 32 strings, each key a letter or digit, then at most 62 letters, digits, dots, underscores or hyphens, each value at most 512 bytes without a control character; any other is invalid_request. The session holds it as given, a fork holds the metadata of the session it forks, and the authorizer's session.create and session.fork carry it as metadata, absent when there is none. The authorizer's allow of session.create or session.fork may attach repositories, each {url, ref, app}, app {id, slug, name, url} the app at the installation's app host it is the source of, which follow the request's resources marked attached, one whose url the request names left out, at most 8 repositories together; and context, titled text {title, text} of at most 32768 bytes together, which the model reads after the initiator's instructions for the session's whole life. An app's id is optional, at most 64 letters, digits, hyphens and underscores, and the session finds the app by it after the app's owner renames it. An app's repository is delivered into the directory of its slug under the working directory, on the session's branch at the commit the app serves. A fork carries the repositories its parent's request named, and what its own allow attaches; a request that names a repository's app or marks one attached is invalid_request. The authorizer's allow of session.create or session.fork may name folder {url, owner, path}, a folder of an Arca-compatible files API: url the API's root, under which files/ and uploads are served, owner the space, and path the folder in that space. The session then keeps the files of its messages and the files its answers show or link in that folder in place of its blobs: a message's file at attachments/<event id>/<name>, and a file an answer of turn N shows or links at results/<N>/<path>, path its place in the working directory, each written once, with the session's own token, and each record names it by ref, its path in the folder, beside blob, its digest, by which the blob route reads it. The session also keeps the latest state of its working directory there, at work/<path>, written at the end of each turn that changed files and recorded by work.saved, and a new machine is restored from it. A file a redaction leaves no live event naming is deleted from the folder. The session answers folder {owner, path} from the first file stored there, and no folder before. A fork copies into its own folder, on the server, each folder of its parent's that its copied events and its message name, and its parent's work/. An allow that names a folder on a server that keeps no files store, or a folder that is not an http or https URL with no user, query or fragment, an owner, and a clean path of two segments or more, is authorizer_unavailable. A file the files service does not take or give is files_unavailable. The authorizer's allow of session.create or session.fork may name memory, at most 4 folders of an Arca-compatible files API, each {name, url, owner, path, access}: name a lowercase letter and at most 31 more lowercase letters, digits or -, unique, url the API's root, owner the space of 1 to 512 bytes, path the folder in that space of at most 512 bytes with no empty, . or .. segment, and access read_only or read_write. The session's read, write, edit, glob and grep reach each folder at /memory/<name>/, with the session's own token, and its commands do not; a write of empty content forgets a file. A folder may name sessions {metadata} in place of url, owner and path, with access read_only: a folder of conversations, one Markdown file per other session of the session's initiator in the session's context that its at most 1 metadata entry keeps (a value the sessions holding the key with it, null those without the key), one per fork tree and never the session's own, named <yyyy-mm-dd>-<session id>.md and holding what the person and the agent said, at most 256 KiB, each list asked session.list and each conversation session.read as the initiator with origin {kind: memory, session_id, folder} and a read with the conversation's metadata. A fork's memory folders are its own allow's, and a rollout's run has none. The session answers memory [{name, access}], without the API's address, the space or the path. An allow that names a folder of a files store on a server that keeps none, or memory that breaks a rule, is authorizer_unavailable. The session runs its agent's model at its agent's reasoning level, and its model is absent from the answer. Where the installation's authorizer names another model or another reasoning level for it, the session starts on that one: its model is {name, via, reasoning, route}, name the model that runs, via the agent's own name for it when the model is another, which a client that offers the choice shows, reasoning the level it runs at, route the routed name the authorizer chose on the way, when it names one, and message_text true when its allow asks for the opening of each later message. A create that carries its first message, a trigger's, asks session.create with the message's shape as a send of a message carries it, and never its opening, since the session has no allow yet. The model that runs is checked after the authorizer is asked: one no source gives an input window and an output limit is model_unknown, and a gateway that does not answer model_unavailable. The session's network is what its machine may reach, network {mode, hosts, ask, source}: mode open, allowlist or none, the one the authorizer's allow names with source authorizer, or the agent's spec.machine egressMode with ask false and source agent. Under allowlist the agent's spec.machine.egress, the hosts of the session's named secrets and the git hosts of its repositories are always joined. A web_fetch of a host inside the network runs without asking, its reason "inside the session's network"; one outside it asks, its reason "outside the session's network", when ask is true and the session is attended, and is blocked otherwise. The allow may carry the initiator's standing instructions, at most 8192 bytes of UTF-8, which the session records as instructions and its model reads after its agent's own; no send changes them. The authorizer's allow of session.create, session.fork and session.send may name the session's connections, at most 32, each {name, kind, title, state, audience, address, git_address, git_url, read_only, hidden, account, api_url, api_example, api_notes}: kind http, an API at address and a git host at git_url reached through git_address from the session's sandbox, or mcp, a remote MCP server at address whose tools the model is offered as mcp__<name>__<tool>. read_only and hidden, of mcp alone, are each at most 64 globs over the server's tool names in path.Match syntax of 1 to 128 bytes: a tool a read_only glob matches reads and every other reaches outside, and a tool a hidden glob matches is never offered to the model, a call of it answered unknown_tool without reaching the server. account, optional, is the account at the other service the connection acts as, one line of at most 256 characters, api_url, optional and of http alone, the service's own API base URL that address stands in for, an https URL, and api_example, optional and of http alone, the whole path of one documented call after api_url, version prefix included, at most 256 bytes with no space, control character, ?, #, $, quote, backtick or backslash, and api_notes, optional and of http alone, one line of at most 800 characters the model is told of the API beyond the example, in which {env} stands for the name of the connection's variable; the model is told each. state is absent for a connected connection, or available for a service the installation offers and the initiator has not connected, which names name, kind and title alone and which the session reaches nothing of; the bound counts both. A create's and a fork's are the session's, a fork's never its parent's, and the session answers them as connections; a send's allow replaces them, appending session.connections_changed {connections} straight before the event when the list differs, and an allow that names none leaves the session with none. An http connection names the audience of TOPOS_CONNECTIONS_AUDIENCE and addresses on the host of TOPOS_CONNECTIONS_URL, and a connection that breaks a rule is authorizer_unavailable naming it. A call of an mcp connection's tool that the connection service answers 409 connection_not_connected, and a drive's listing of its tools that meets it, append connection.requested {name, title, kind, reason, scopes, tool_use_id}, tool_use_id absent for a listing, which a client shows the person as a service to connect again. While the session has an available connection, of kind mcp or, on a Cella machine, http, the session's own model, not a subagent's, is offered request_connection {name, reason}, whose call appends connection.requested {name, title, kind, reason, tool_use_id}, reason the model's sentence on what it needs the service for, which a client shows the person as a service to connect. The body's machine names a person's own computer for the session to work on, {kind: device, environment, workdir}: environment the name of the Cella environment the computer serves, a DNS label, and workdir the folder on it the session works in, an absolute, clean path of at most 4096 bytes with no control character. Any other kind, and any other member, is invalid_request, and a server without Cella is machine_unavailable. The session records it as its machine for its whole life. session.create carries machine device with environment and workdir, so the authorizer decides whether the person the session acts for may use that computer; a fork of the session carries the same three in session.fork, decided for the person forking, and a fork the authorizer refuses is not created. A trigger names a device the same way in spec.session.machine, the one machine a trigger names; its trigger.create and trigger.update carry machine device with environment and workdir, so the authorizer decides whether the person applying it may use that computer when it is applied, as well as at each firing's session.create, and the sessions a trigger starts record trigger_fires_on, schedule or events. The session's sandbox is created on that environment with the folder bound in place as its workspace and working directory, with no image, no Secret, no LUX_URL and no HOME, labeled topos.latere.ai/agent-version and, for a session a trigger started, topos.latere.ai/trigger and topos.latere.ai/trigger-fires-on, and annotated topos.latere.ai/agent-name with the agent's display name, which the computer shows its owner. No repository is delivered into the folder, the files of a message are written under topos/attachments/ in the sandbox's temporary directory, and the session keeps no checkpoint and no copy of its working directory and restores neither, so a rewind finds no checkpoint. A call there scores as a call on a host and is decided in confirm mode when the session runs progressive, by the agent's manifest or a change of the mode: a call that reads runs, and any other asks unless always_allow names it or the person allowed it earlier in the session with remember, plan still blocks a change, and each agent.tool_use records mode confirm. The model's requests carry prompt_version harness/4. The body's rollout, the id of the rollout the session is one run of, a letter or digit then at most 127 letters, digits, dots, underscores or hyphens, and neither none nor any, is the session's for its whole life, and session.create carries it as rollout. A rollout's runs are left out of the session list, the search and the summary unless their rollout parameter names the rollout or any, and no person attends them: a call that would wait for a person's confirmation is answered at once as denied, and the session does not wait. A run reaches none of its initiator's accounts or context: whatever its allow names, it holds no instructions, no context, no attached repository and no connection, a send's allow changes no connection of it, its sandbox holds no token of the connection service, and none is minted for it; its network, its folder and the repositories its body names are its allow's and its body's, as any session's. A sender who did not start the session names a file of the session's own space alone, the owner of the session's folder, and a source of any other space from them, me among them, is attachment_source_not_found before anything is read. The copy leaves out the directories .git, node_modules, bower_components, .venv, venv, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .nox, .cache, .npm, .pnpm-store, .yarn, .gradle, .m2, target, .terraform, .turbo, .parcel-cache at any depth, what the credential deny-list names, and anything that is no regular file. A fork's first work.saved, whole with from its parent's id, names every file of the copy it starts from, its parent's latest. The blob route does not answer a file of the copy. A session on a person's own computer stops with stop_reason machine_waiting, the reason, offline or approval, in its session.status detail, when the computer is offline or asleep, or when its owner has not allowed the session within 2 minutes of a call's asking, the create left waiting on the computer; session.machine_waiting {reason, environment} names the reason, appended when a call begins to wait for the owner, which a client shows as a request to allow the session on the computer, and when a turn stops for a computer that is offline, so the last one names why the session waits. A computer that stops answering under a call stops the turn the same way, reason offline. A computer whose owner refused the session, or did not answer in time, appends session.error {code: machine_refused, message: "The computer did not allow this session.", detail}, detail the computer's own words; the call is answered so, and so is every later call of the turn that acts on the machine, and the turn goes on. The next user.message, or a resume, continues a session idle on machine_waiting on the same computer. Each model.request of a step, the session's own or a subagent's, or of a compaction records context {window, used, source, parts}: window the model's input window from the catalog, 0 when it names none; used the input tokens the request used, source provider when the response counted its prompt tokens and estimate when it did not, as a failed or cut request, where used is the harness's estimate; and parts [{part, tokens}] in the order instructions, tools, messages, files, summary, free, each the harness's estimate scaled so the parts but free sum to used, and free the window less used. A title's request records none. The session folds the latest of its own conversation's as context_report. agent.tool_use and approval.requested record attended: false on a turn a trigger's message began, a wake's included, and in a subagent that turn drove; true on a turn a person's message, answer or confirmation began. Such a turn decides without the patterns the session's confirmations remembered; always_allow, always_confirm, the mode and a decision service decide as on any turn, and a decision service reads attended in the action's attributes. budget.spent_cost_usd_micro is what the session's log cost through last_seq: the cost_usd_micro of every model.request, the session's own and each subagent's, a compaction's and a title's included, and of every tool.result a service charged for, such as a web_search or a PDF a read took as text, a redacted result's from its tombstone; no other event adds to it. A client that read the session keeps the spending current by adding the cost_usd_micro of each model.request and tool.result after last_seq as the stream carries it, which is the next read's spent_cost_usd_micro. A fork's spent_cost_usd_micro counts the events it copied, which carried_cost_usd_micro holds apart: its own spending, which its max_cost_usd_micro caps, is spent less carried.

get.description: List the triggers the list would, each with its runs since since, the mean cost of its latest runs, and the times it fires up to until, so a client can forecast what they will cost. A run is a firing that started or continued a turn, with what the turn cost as a look is counted, or one skipped_budget, skipped_nothing_new or refused stopped, with no cost; ended says the turn closed and its cost is final. A firing of a trigger whose reach splits by scope is a run per scope it started or the authorizer refused, each naming its scope and costing what its own session's turn cost. A wake's runs are the wake runs of its session, each once its own trigger; any other trigger's are its own and the wake runs of the sessions it started, which count toward its allowance. runs holds at most 3000, the newest, more_runs saying older ones were left out. per_run_usd_micro is the mean cost of the latest 5 of its own runs that ran and ended, from every run kept, which is 42 days. fires_on is schedule, event, at for a one-shot, or times for a list of times. fires are the times it fires after now and before until, as the minute loop fires them: a schedule's in its zone, a one-shot's time, or for a one-shot past its time that waits, the next pass for its allowance or the moment the limit that refused it resets; a list's times still to come, after the next try of one of them that waits, as a one-shot's; none for an event trigger or a suspended one. The hold is not applied. At most 3000, the soonest, more_fires saying later ones were left out. target names the one session a wake or a trigger naming session.target continues, and the trigger that started it, absent for a session a person started. The read records each firing since since that is a run and has none, and completes a run whose turn had not ended from its session's log. trigger.list is asked as the list asks it.

put.description: Apply a Trigger manifest to the caller's own trigger of the name; the caller becomes its owner. The body is one Trigger manifest of topos.latere.ai/v1. It fires on spec.schedule, a five-field cron expression or @hourly, @daily, @weekly read in spec.timeZone, or on the events spec.on selects: product exactly, verbs and resources each exact or a prefix ending in *, and match rules {path, in} on the payload. spec.session.message, title and key, and a repository's url and ref, are templates of {{event.*}}, {{trigger.id}}, {{trigger.name}}, {{firing.id}} and {{firing.time}}; each value is cut at 16384 bytes and a message past 65536 bytes refuses its firing. spec.session.policy new starts a session per firing, skipped while the key's session is active under skipIfActive; continue sends each firing to the key's open session, held while it waits for a person. At most spec.maxActive sessions, 5 by default and 100 at most, are active at once. The caller becomes the trigger's owner, the initiator of every session it starts, and a firing is asked of the authorizer as the owner in the context the caller's token names. trigger.create and trigger.update carry the trigger's name, its agent and the filter applied as on, and, when spec.session.machine names a person's own computer, {kind: device, environment, workdir}, machine device with environment and workdir beside them, as session.create carries them. spec.at, an RFC 3339 time with an offset in place of schedule and on, fires the trigger once, and its firing spends it: the server deletes it with the firing that started, continued, skipped or refused, and keeps it while that firing is held or runs again after it failed; trigger.create and trigger.update carry at. spec.times, a list of 1 to 100 RFC 3339 times with an offset in place of schedule, on and at, none the same instant as another, fires the trigger once at each, as at fires: each time is a firing of its own, late past maxAge or once the next listed time has come, and one refused for a limit that resets waits for it no later than the next listed time; the firing of the latest time spends the trigger as at's does, and an earlier time's firing keeps it. A time already past may stay in the list and never fires, so a list read back applies again as it is, but a list with no time after now is invalid_manifest. status.nextFireAt is the next listed time to fire, or when one that waits is tried again. A manual fire runs once now and spends no listed time. trigger.create and trigger.update carry times, each in RFC 3339 in UTC, in the list's order. spec.timeZone beside at or times is the zone a client shows them in. spec.session.target, under policy continue and beside no key, names the open session of spec.agent every firing sends its message to, which the caller may send to; a firing whose target has ended or is gone is skipped_ended. A session's wake is such a trigger, applied by the session's wake tool as the session's initiator with status.origin {kind: wake}: at least 10 minutes and at most 168 hours ahead and inside its session's life, and skipped_late past 24 hours; its firing's user.message carries wake {trigger_id, set_at, due_at, count}, count from 1. status.paused {why, by, sessionId, toolUseId, at} says who suspended the trigger and when, with the agent's why and its call for a pause a session's call made; it is kept while the trigger stays suspended and cleared when it resumes. spec.session.attended makes each session a firing starts attended, so its questions wait for the owner; session.create is asked with attended. spec.session.notify is always, the default, or judged: a firing of a judged trigger sends its message with notify judged, and the turn it begins records outcome quiet on its closing status unless the agent calls its notify tool or waits for the person; judged is refused for an agent whose latest version does not name notify. trigger.create and trigger.update carry notify. spec.session.model, {"name": "<model>", "reasoning": "<level>"} with either member or both, the shape a session's change of its model takes, is the model each session a firing starts begins on in place of its agent's, and its reasoning level, one of minimal, low, medium, high; a member left out is the agent's. session.create is asked with its name as model, and its level under both reasoning and effort when it names one, as a create that names its model is, and the session runs as it would on its agent's own model: on the model the allow names in its place, with the trigger's name as via, at the level the allow names when it names one. A firing that continues an open session sends its message and leaves the model that session runs, and a trigger under session.target ignores spec.session.model. A model that names neither member, a name with space around it, or another level is invalid_manifest. spec.budget.perWeek, an integer of USD micros above zero, is the most the looks counted toward the trigger may cost in a rolling 7 days: a look is a turn a firing's message began, counted from that message through the turn's closing status, and the looks counted are the trigger's own, in the sessions it started or continued, and the ones wakes began in the sessions it started. A firing while that spend is at or past the allowance starts nothing and records skipped_budget, counted as skippedBudget; a one-shot, a wake included, keeps its time and is tried again each minute until it fires or maxAge passes, and no firing needs a resume. trigger.create and trigger.update carry budget {per_week_usd_micro}. status.spend {windowDays, spentUsdMicro, perWeekUsdMicro, perLookUsdMicro, expectedLooks, projectedUsdMicro} is written at each firing that counts toward the trigger, before its look: perLookUsdMicro the mean of the window's latest 5 looks that ended, expectedLooks the looks expected from the firing to the end of the window that the oldest counted look opened, and projectedUsdMicro spent plus perLook times expectedLooks. The firing's user.message carries the same numbers as spend {trigger_id, window_days, spent_usd_micro, per_week_usd_micro, per_look_usd_micro, expected_looks, projected_usd_micro}, trigger_id the trigger counted toward, for a wake the trigger that started its session. A session's trigger tool writes spec.budget.perWeek from its perWeekUsd, the agent's estimate of a week of looks. spec.reach {kind, split} names what the trigger's runs reach as a kind matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}$, which the authorizer maps and the server decides nothing from: trigger.create and trigger.update carry reach {kind, split}, split left out when absent, and each firing's session.create carries reach {kind}. split scope, for a trigger on spec.schedule under policy new with no session.target and no session.key, runs each firing once per due scope: before it starts anything the firing asks trigger.runs as the owner, with the trigger's owner, name and agent, reach, firing {id, at, origin} and last {<scope>: <RFC 3339>}, each scope's latest run of the trigger that started a session. The allow's limits name the scopes due in the order they start, {"runs": [{"scope": "you", "since": "<RFC 3339>"}]}, since optional: at most 16, each matching ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_./:-]{0,127}$, none twice, or the firing is refused runs_invalid. A deny refuses the firing with its reason. An allow that names none records skipped_nothing_new, counted as skippedNothingNew: a run that cost nothing, with no session and no model call. Each scope due starts a session keyed by the scope, its session.create carrying reach {kind, scope, since}; a scope whose session is still active is passed over under skipIfActive and recorded nowhere, and maxActive bounds no scope. The firing records started with its first session, refused with the first reason when no scope started and one was refused, failed when every start tried failed, and skipped_active when every scope was passed over; each started or refused scope is a run of its own, and every session of the firing counts toward the allowance together.
